chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
"Any man who makes a vow to walk to the House of God, then becomes unable to walk, should ride and offer a camel, when God knows sufficient effort from him."
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a failed vow to walk to the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that physical inability to fulfill a vow of walking to the Kaaba permits substitution with riding, accompanied by the sacrifice of a camel (*badanah*) as expiation. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of *al-jahd* (capacity), ensuring that vows remain attainable and not burdensome, while the specific requirement of a camel reflects the pre-Islamic and early Islamic context of wealth-based expiations. The ruling underscores the flexibility in *Nudhur* (vows) to accommodate changing circumstances without invalidating the vow's spiritual intent.
